text:
Maya (Support): FYI customer FinEdge reports a wire was returned this morning. amount: $125,000 USD. bank return note: 'CORR_BIC_UNRECOGNIZED - intermediary BIC CORRUS33 not recognized by beneficiary bank (requires 8-char BIC)'. payment_id: pay_0a7f9c. trace: 8d3f2b1c. Can Payments team confirm if we sent CORRUS33 or if a mapping should have occurred?
payment-processing-bot: Payment pay_0a7f9c status updated -> RETURNED. Auto-refund queued, ETA 24-48h. Notifying ops.
Jonah (Payments): @Maya can you paste the outgoing envelope (the MT103 / API payload) and the routing-selection log for that payment? Need quick repro. Also what's customer SLA window?
Maya (Support): Copy of API payload below (sanitized):
```json
{
  "payment_id": "pay_0a7f9c",
  "amount": 125000.00,
  "currency": "USD",
  "beneficiary": {"name": "FinEdge Inc","iban": "US89 1234 0000 0000 0000 01"},
  "intermediary_bic": "CORRUS33",
  "beneficiary_bank_bic": "BENEBANKX"
}
```
Bank response (SWIFT relay):
```
REJECT: CORR_BIC_UNRECOGNIZED - "Intermediary BIC 'CORRUS33' not recognised; beneficiary requires 8-char BIC format or 'CORRUS3X' as replacement"
```
Priya (Oncall Eng): Thanks. I grabbed the routing selection logs for pay_0a7f9c: we selected route v3 -> intermediary CORRUS33 from routing-table v2026-11-07. Looks like we have a deprecated mapping that should normalize CORRUS33 -> CORRUS3X but transformation didn't run. Repro steps:
1) curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routing/lookup?bic=CORRUS33"
2) check transform: /etc/routing/mappings.d/corrus-maps.yaml

Example log snippet:
```
2026-11-07T09:12:44Z route_select:bic=CORRUS33 table=v2026-11-07 transform_applied=false matched_rule=deprecated_bic_map
```
Carlos (Ops): I think I see the problem: our normalization pipeline strips trailing whitespace and lowercases BICs, but one of the mapping keys had an accidental non-breaking space at the end so the normalization didn't match. That mapping points CORRUS33 -> CORRUS3X (replacement). Fix: remove NBSP, reload routing cache. Commands: 
```
# fix mapping file (ops)
sed -i 's/\xC2\xA0//g' /etc/routing/mappings.d/corrus-maps.yaml
redwoodctl config reload routing && curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/cache/flush/routing -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPSTOKEN"
```
Jonah (Payments): After reload, resubmit with adjusted intermediary_bic=CORRUS3X. If customer needs same-day settlement tell them we can attempt reissue but beneficiary may charge fees. Escalation checklist for support: 
- Mark ticket P1 and include ledger trace 8d3f2b1c
- Confirm mapping reload (ops) and paste success log
- Ask customer to confirm whether beneficiary wants BIC CORRUS3X or an account-level correction
- If we reissue, include remittance_id and annotate 'Resubmitted after intermediary BIC normalization'
Priya (Oncall Eng): I'll validate transform runs on prod in staging first. If all good I'll trigger cache flush and post the reload confirmation here.
Maya (Support): OK I'll tell FinEdge: we're investigating, will attempt to resubmit after ops reloads routing table. Asked them to hold funds on their side. ETA update in 1h. :thumbsup:
Carlos (Ops): routing reload done: "routing service v2026-11-07 reloaded, 1 mapping cleaned (corrus-maps.yaml)". Cache flush returned 200.
Jonah (Payments): Great. @Maya proceed with reissue flow. Include original trace id and set customer_fee_waiver = true. I'm opening payments ticket #PAY-8742 and cc'ing Treasury.
Maya (Support): Noted. Customer notified. Will follow up when reissue completes.
